name: LinkUTM
tagline: A builder and library for tagged campaign URLs, so marketing links stay consistent instead of turning into fifty spellings of 'newsletter'.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: A UTM builder is string concatenation with a taste police attached. The hard part is not the URL, it is enforcing one spelling of each source, medium and campaign and keeping a searchable history of what you already shipped. An agent can produce that in a single sitting: a form, a controlled vocabulary you define once, validation that rejects spaces and uppercase, a saved library with search, and CSV export into whatever spreadsheet your reports live in. What you do not get for free is the team layer, the browser extension, and the short-link redirects some of these tools bolt on. If you are one person or a small crew tagging your own links, the paid tier is buying you discipline you could also just encode in a local app.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you pick from your own approved source/medium/campaign vocabulary, generate a validated tagged URL, copy it, and keep a searchable, exportable history of every link you have ever built.
requirements: A decision, made once, about your own UTM naming convention
Somewhere to host it if more than one person needs the same vocabulary
whatYouLose: Shared team taxonomy with real accounts, so two people cannot drift into 'email' and 'Email' from separate laptops
A browser extension or bookmarklet that tags the page you are already looking at
Built-in short links and redirect hosting, which is a whole separate service if you want it
Integrations that push the link library into Sheets, ad platforms or analytics tools automatically
Someone else owning uptime for URLs that are printed in live campaigns
moatNotes: The durable part is not the generator, it is being the single place a whole marketing team agrees to look up naming. Solo, that agreement is free.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because UTM chaos is a people problem, not a code problem, and a hosted tool with logins is a cheap way to force a convention on coworkers who will not read your README. Teams also want the extension, the short links and the export hooks in one place, plus a link history that survives someone's laptop dying mid-campaign. If you are tagging links for three clients and four channels by yourself, none of that is worth a subscription. If eight people are tagging and your attribution reports are already garbage, paying for the referee is rational.
notes: The entire product is a query string with manners, but the manners are the point.
prompt:
Build a local-first UTM link builder and library. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable: Vite + React + TypeScript, plain CSS, no UI framework. All data in browser localStorage under one namespaced key. Single page app, runs with `npm run dev`. No backend.

Core features:
1. A Vocabulary screen where I define allowed values for utm_source, utm_medium and utm_campaign, plus optional utm_term and utm_content. Each value has a label and the exact lowercase slug that goes in the URL. Stored locally, editable, deletable.
2. A Builder screen: base URL input, then dropdowns for source, medium, campaign (picked from my vocabulary, not free text), and optional free-text term/content that gets slugified.
3. Live preview of the final URL. Copy button. Validation that blocks: missing protocol, spaces, uppercase in any utm value, duplicate query keys, and base URLs that already contain utm_ params (offer to strip them).
4. Save to a Library: every generated link stored with all params broken out, a note field, and createdAt. Library has full-text search, filter by source/medium/campaign, sort by date, copy, and delete.
5. Duplicate detection: if the exact same tagged URL already exists in the library, say so instead of saving twice.
6. Export the library to CSV (one column per utm param plus full URL and note) and to JSON. Import the same JSON back for backup and restore.
7. A slugify helper used everywhere: lowercase, trim, spaces and underscores to hyphens, strip anything not a-z0-9-.

Explicitly out of scope: short links, redirects, click tracking, analytics dashboards, browser extension, multi-user accounts, any third-party API.

Deliverables: working app, a seed vocabulary with sensible defaults (source: newsletter, twitter, linkedin; medium: email, social, cpc, referral), and a README with run instructions and a one-paragraph note that all data lives in this browser only. No .env needed because there are no secrets.
